class.name: VoxelVolume3D
class.brief_description: Puts a [VoxelField] in a scene, drawing what it holds and optionally colliding with it.
class.description: A [VoxelVolume3D] draws the mesh a [VoxelField] extracts, and moves it with the node. Assign a field to [member field] and whatever is stamped into that field appears here, re-extracted as it changes with nothing to call in between. The node's transform positions the volume in the world; it does not reach inside the field. Positions passed to the field stay in the field's own space, so a volume can be moved, rotated, or reparented at any time without invalidating a single coordinate a caller is holding. Turn on [member collision_enabled] to have the volume keep a static collision body in step with the field. One field may be shared by several volumes, which is how the same carved object is drawn twice without extracting it twice. [codeblock] var volume := VoxelVolume3D.new() volume.field = my_field volume.collision_enabled = true volume.set_surface_override_material(0, my_material) add_child(volume) [/codeblock]

method.name: get_collision_shape
method.description: Returns the [VoxelShape3D] the volume keeps while [member collision_enabled] is on, or [code]null[/code] otherwise. The shape is managed by the volume; it is exposed for inspection and for drawing debug geometry, not to be swapped out.

method.name: get_surface_override_material
method.description: Returns the material assigned to one surface, or [code]null[/code] if that surface has none.

method.name: get_surface_override_material_count
method.description: Returns how many surfaces the field currently extracts, which is one per material ID present in it. This grows on its own when a cut exposes a material that was not visible before.

method.name: set_surface_override_material
method.description: Assigns a [Material] to one of the field's surfaces. Surface indices follow the material IDs present in the field, so surface [code]0[/code] is the lowest ID in use. Assignments are kept across re-extraction and across a surface count that changes, so a material can be set for a surface a cut has not yet exposed and it will be there when the cut exposes it.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], the volume keeps a static collision body matching the field's surface, re-extracted as the field changes. Off by default, because collision is the more expensive half of a stamp and plenty of volumes are only ever looked at.
The physics layers this volume's collision body is in. See [member CollisionObject3D.collision_layer].
The physics layers this volume's collision body scans. See [member CollisionObject3D.collision_mask].

How many voxels wide one collision cell is, so [code]4[/code] builds collision at a quarter of the resolution the volume is drawn at. Raising it makes stamps cheaper and physics faster while letting collision round off detail that remains visible. Defaults to [member ProjectSettings.voxel/collision/voxel_multiplier].

The field this volume draws. Assigning one connects the volume to it, and any stamp into that field shows up here without the volume being told. Several volumes may share one field. The field is not owned by the volume, so it outlives being unassigned.

How far, in pixels on screen, a lower detail level may deviate from the full-resolution surface before the volume refuses it. [b]Note:[/b] Accepted and stored, but nothing reads it yet: the volume always draws at full resolution. It is here so that scenes written now do not have to be revisited when levels of detail arrive.
